newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Telkom dollars sold forward for May 22.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Telkom dollars sold forward for May 22.

text.p: A total of $1 billion due to South African telecommunications utility Telkom following its part-privatisation has been sold forward for delivery on May 22 or shortly after, a Finance Ministry official said on Monday.

South Africa is due to close a deal for the sale of 30 percent of state-run Telkom to a U.S.-Malaysian consortium at 1500 GMT on Wednesday in Cape Town, after which there will be an exchange of cash for shares.
U.S.-based SBC Communications Inc and Telekom Malaysia Bhd are acquiring the stake in Telkom for $1.26 billion, the biggest direct investment in South Africa to date.

Some $260 million of the amount will go to the exchequer to retire state debt and will not impact the market. But $1 billion will be deposited in Telkom's private sector bank account to help fund infrastructure growth -- a move that could impact directly on the money market.
Koen Kruger, head of asset management at the Ministry of Finance, said the $1.26 billion would be paid into an offshore banking account on either Wednesday or Thursday this week.
But there would be no immediate currency market impact as the $1 billion due to Telkom had been sold forward.
"The $1 billion dollar amount that will accrue to Telkom has been sold forward to the Reserve Bank for delivery on May 22 or thereabouts," he told Reuters.

"The Reserve Bank will then simply pay the rand into the acount of Telkom at the predetermined rate. Obviously it will have an impact on the money market but the Reserve Bank, through its normal market activities, will smooth the position.
"The aim is to smooth the effects on the exchange rate and the domestic money market."
